presentation.label: QPER LIVE REC
presentation.summary: Set performance locks by holding QPER and turning knobs, apply them to the kit, and record performance moves in LIVE RECORDING.
presentation.overview: Hold QPER and turn a knob: it edits that parameter's offset in the performance linked to QPER, and the knob inverts and shows it as it does for a held performance pad. QPER + PLAY clears it and PLAY again undoes that. QPER + RECORD and STOP copy and paste it. QPER + YES writes what you hear into the kit and removes those locks. In LIVE RECORDING the pads, the QPER knob and MIDI performance moves are kept in a quick perf rec that loops with the pattern; RECORD + YES writes it into the pattern as locks, RECORD + NO clears it.
highlights: Sets a lock in the linked performance with one turn
QPER + PLAY clears the linked performance
QPER + YES moves them into the kit
Records pad and QPER knob moves in LIVE RECORDING and plays them back, 8 points a step
usage: Hold QPER, press pad 1 to link its performance, and keep holding.
Turn FLTR's cutoff up and the resonance a little, and let go of QPER.
Sweep the QPER knob. Both moves come in together.
When a position sounds right, hold QPER and press YES to keep it in the kit.
Hold QPER and press RECORD, press pad 2, then STOP to start another performance from this one.
Press PERF, hold RECORD and press PLAY. While the pattern plays, press and squeeze pads 1 and 2. Let go and listen to the next pass.
Hold RECORD and press YES to write the moves into the pattern.

access.location: The QPER key, on the sound pages and in PERF, SCNE, MUTE and CHRO.
steps: Hold QPER and press a pad to link that one performance.
Keep QPER held and turn a knob to set its offset.
QPER + PLAY clears the linked performance; press PLAY again to undo. QPER + RECORD copies it, QPER + STOP pastes.
QPER + YES moves them into the kit.
In PERF mode, hold RECORD and press PLAY, then play the pads: the moves loop. RECORD + YES writes them into the pattern; RECORD + NO empties them, NO again undoes.

limitations: A press with QPER held leaves one link, unlike stock. A kit with several keeps them until then, and shows MORE THAN ONE LINKED.
The gestures work on the sound pages and in PERF, SCNE, MUTE and CHRO, not in menus.
Until the QPER knob moves after power on, QPER + YES uses the amounts stock holds.
Replaces stock's QPER + PLAY, which starts the sequencer.
Recorded performance moves live in RAM until QPER + YES writes them: a pattern change, project load or power off drops them.
The move lane holds 64 steps; a track at its own speed gets no locks from it.

load.display: About 0.5 % of the audio block idle (the audio handler, measured on a unit)
load.conditions: Measured on an Analog Rytm MKII, the audio handler timed on DTIM0. 0.2.0 in the author's 16-module set, stopped: 8.7 us a block before its idle early return, 5.1 us after; removing the module lowered the idle block from 72.9 % to 70.9 %. 0.2.2 alone against 0.2.1 on the same unit and kit: 3.6 us a block stopped (0.53 %, 0.2.1 0.97 %) and 6.8 us playing (1.03 %, 0.2.1 1.45 %). With moves to record, a pad held or a take playing back it runs in full each block.

hardware.summary: 0.3.0 ran alone on npp1993's Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, from RAM as QU02 (the Modwerk base with the development link and this module; sha256 dccd518a…ceb1, src/main.c sha256 2e6f97f9…0160). Four rig cases, run over the USB link with no hand on the unit, read the take from RAM: a 16-step take repeated over steps 17-32 when the SCALE menu took the master length to 32 one step at a time, 16 to 24 repeated steps 1-8, 32 scrolled down to INF kept the take and repeated it over 33-64, a cleared take stayed as it was until NO brought it back filled to 32, and RECORD + YES after a lengthening showed APPLY QUICK PERF REC and made a 16-step track 32 steps.
limitations: Run by the rig over the USB link, not by a person: no pads, pressure, QPER knob, LEDs or sound.
The image holds the base with the development link, not the plain published base.
The cases ran one after another on one pattern, so two checks that assumed empty steps past the loop read moves left by the case before.

tests.summary: The author's Analog Rytm MKII, with a USB MIDI trace for the quick perf rec, and rytm-emu. 0.3.0 (the take repeats when the loop gets longer): host scenarios, rytm-emu, and four rig cases on the author's unit that read the take from RAM; RECORD + YES after a lengthening applied on the unit. 0.2.2: no difference from 0.2.1 in 80 million host blocks, and 470 ticks a block stopped on the unit against 850. 0.2.1 passed the tutorial on the author's unit alone (QR01). TESTING.md names each build.
